title: White-label branding governance and protected legal terms
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (REQ-X-030, REQ-X-029, UNB-RCN-PLT-007, UNB-PLAT-009); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Each sponsor has one governed, versioned Brand Kit (identity, logos, accessible design tokens, typography, terminology, approved assets, support contacts, channel policies) applied consistently to donor portals, administrative interfaces, embedded components, email and Folio documents. Publication validates terminology overrides against a protected-term registry of legally meaningful terms (grant recommendation, sponsoring organization legal name, acknowledgment wording) whose meaning may not be altered, and validates contrast and accessibility of brand tokens. Branding never hides the sponsor's legal identity.

intended_practice: Brand Kit per REQ-X-030 and REQ-X-029, protected terms per UNB-RCN-PLT-007, design system per UNB-PLAT-009 (Forma and Folio).

title: Co-branded disclosures, legal meaning and platform registration
status_rationale: State platform registration obligations depend on counsel interpretation of the deployment model; requirements specify the intended approach but no registration or disclosure exists.
target_answer: In co-branded and partner channels the sponsor is always identified as the legal owner of contributed assets and the party that decides grants; partner copy about sponsor actions is reviewed for legal meaning (donors recommend, the sponsor approves and pays). Partners may display sponsor financial figures only through sponsor widgets or signed data with as-of times. Before white-label, embedded or charity-side donation features are activated for California or Hawaii users, Unbound registers as a charitable fundraising platform with those states' attorneys general and meets the associated disclosure and recordkeeping duties. Email sender identity follows message classification.

title: Embedded component security: framing, CSP, message validation and launch tokens
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (INT-015, AIN-029, MON-022, WG-1); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Embedded components run on a sponsor-controlled widget origin, never inherit host authority, and treat the host page as untrusted. Launch uses a one-use, short-lived launch artifact obtained by the partner backend with a server credential for a mapped subject; the widget sets an exact CSP frame-ancestors allowlist per registered host origin; postMessage traffic is validated by origin and schema and carries only opaque host events; every command is reauthorized server-side at execution. Authority changes clear displayed data within a stated window, review steps resist overlay (visibility checks where supported) and high-value or new-recipient actions hand off to a top-level window. Application JavaScript runs only through the Limen boundary.
current_practice: Not established. Unbound is requirements-only with no production system, customers or operating evidence (unbound@9b38de47).
intended_practice: Widget trust contract per INT-015, AIN-029, MON-022 and the widget integration model (WG-1..WG-9); revocation per UNB-RCN-WF-013 and TVR-WID-001; SEC-UI-002 (Limen).
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text exists in unbound@9b38de47 (requirements/baseline/baseline.jsonl); no implementation, test execution or operating evidence.
customer_statement: Planned, not available today: embedded components would use one-use launch tokens, strict frame-ancestors allowlists, validated messages and server-side reauthorization. Unbound has no production deployment; this describes intended design only.
external_assurance: None. No SOC report, audit, penetration test or independent review covers this area.
owner: Unbound product owner (proposed role; not yet assigned)

W3C Content Security Policy is not a seeded source.

challenge.customer_intent: Sponsors and banks want embedded giving without exposing donors to clickjacking, session theft or host-page compromise.
challenge.adverse_outcome: A compromised or malicious host page induces grants, reads donor data or keeps a revoked advisor's view alive.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Conventional assurance relies on partner security questionnaires and annual pen tests of the host, which do not constrain what a compromised host can do.
challenge.legally_required: No statute prescribes embedding controls; bank partners will apply their third-party risk management expectations.
challenge.contractually_required: Partner agreements commonly require security attestations.
challenge.historical_convention: Vendors offer iframes with permissive framing and rely on partner security.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Widget never inherits host authority and partners receive only opaque events, so host compromise cannot reach sponsor data or authority beyond what the user sees.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Exact frame-ancestors, origin-validated messaging, one-use launch artifacts and server-side reauthorization enforced by the platform.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Launch, revocation and command reauthorization events are logged per partner.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Architectural containment of the host rather than reliance on host security.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, through browser-level tests and adversarial testing; not yet performed.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely, if supported by an independent penetration test.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Overlay detection (IntersectionObserver v2) is not universally supported; Limen does not yet support element or shadow-root roots, forcing iframe or web-component interim designs.
challenge.conventional_cost: Medium recurring cost for partner assessments.
challenge.alternative_risks: Third-party cookie restrictions and browser changes can break embedded sessions.
supporting_arguments: Containment does not depend on partner diligence
Limits blast radius of host compromise
opposing_arguments: Clickjacking defenses are incomplete in some browsers
Interim design pending Limen root support

title: Partner segregation and tenant isolation
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-TEN-001, UNB-TEN-002, UNB-TEN-003, UNB-TEN-004); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: The tenant unit is the legal sponsor; every authoritative record carries immutable tenant, sponsor and program context. Partner and program isolation inside a sponsor cell is enforced by typed partitioning and negative tests, and a partner needing dedicated infrastructure is served by a dedicated sponsor cell or separate legal sponsor. Isolation profiles (shared database with separate schemas, dedicated database, dedicated infrastructure) are selectable per sponsor and recorded over time. Tenant routing derives from verified identity, never a client value, and isolation extends to caches, queues, event streams, search indexes, backups and telemetry. Shared services carry no donor PII beyond a registered shared-store list.
current_practice: Not established. Unbound is requirements-only with no production system, customers or operating evidence (unbound@9b38de47).
intended_practice: Tenancy per UNB-TEN-001..020, CNV-TEN-001, CNV-ARC-002, UNB-XIN-SAS-005; custodian isolation per UNB-CUST-019.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text exists in unbound@9b38de47 (requirements/baseline/baseline.jsonl); no implementation, test execution or operating evidence.
customer_statement: Planned, not available today: partners and sponsors would be isolated by verified tenant context with negative tests across every data store. Unbound has no production deployment; this describes intended design only.

challenge.customer_intent: Financial institution partners want assurance that no other partner can see their clients.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Cross-partner data exposure, a reportable incident and contract breach.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Questionnaire answers and annual pen tests sample isolation but do not prove it continuously.
challenge.legally_required: Not prescribed by statute; GLBA safeguards and bank TPRM expectations apply to bank partners' data.
challenge.contractually_required: Bank partners commonly require dedicated or demonstrably segregated environments.
challenge.historical_convention: Dedicated instances per large client or row-level tenant filters.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Tenant context derived from verified identity and typed partitioning remove client-controlled tenant selection.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Every query path goes through a tenant connection broker; negative tests run continuously.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Isolation profile history and negative test results per tenant.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Typed tenancy plus continuous negative testing rather than dedicated hardware by default.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, through negative test evidence and penetration testing.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Uncertain; some banks will still require dedicated infrastructure regardless of evidence.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Shared services, backups or support tooling outside the broker could bypass isolation.
challenge.conventional_cost: High for dedicated infrastructure per partner.
challenge.alternative_risks: Logical isolation errors affect all tenants in a shared cell.
supporting_arguments: Evidence of isolation is continuous rather than sampled

title: Partner access to donor data and event minimization
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-XIN-EVA-008, TVR-WID-002, AUTH-I8, WG-7); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Partners receive the minimum data necessary: domain events are classified private or published, and published integration events are a separately versioned contract carrying opaque references rather than financial details. Partners display sponsor financial data only through sponsor widgets or signed data with as-of times. Partner identity mapping uses a permanent identifier (issuer and subject or SCIM external ID), and mapping changes require dual control and donor notice. On partner offboarding, the partner attests deletion of any data received. No partner appears in the funds flow.

intended_practice: Event classification per UNB-XIN-EVA-008, figure display per TVR-WID-002, identity mapping per AUTH-I8, offboarding per WG-7, funds flow per UNB-XIN-OTH-003.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text exists in unbound@9b38de47 (requirements/baseline/baseline.jsonl); no implementation, test execution or operating evidence.

challenge.customer_intent: Sponsors want partners to serve donors without becoming an uncontrolled copy of donor data.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Partner breach or misuse exposes donor giving data.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Contract clauses and partner security questionnaires do not limit what data partners hold.
challenge.legally_required: No statute prescribes minimization here; privacy laws and GLBA principles favor it where applicable.
challenge.historical_convention: Vendors provide partners full data feeds or APIs.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Partners never receive financial details by design; there is nothing to leak beyond opaque references.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Published event contract excludes sensitive fields; schema checks in the build.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Published event schemas and partner data access logs.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Minimization by contract design rather than by partner diligence.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, by schema review and data access logs.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Uncertain; some partners want full data for their own CRM and advice.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If partners demand data for advice or reporting, pressure to widen the event contract will arise.
challenge.alternative_risks: Partners may build screen-scraping or other workarounds.
supporting_arguments: Reduces partner breach impact to near zero for financial data
opposing_arguments: Wealth-management partners need holdings data for advice

title: Partner API access, entitlements and deprovisioning
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-API-002, UNB-API-003, UNB-API-004, UNB-API-006); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Partner APIs authenticate partner backends with scoped server credentials and authorize every call against the partner's per-tenant capability entitlements; external writes express requests, never approvals, money movement or policy publication. Mutating commands require idempotency keys and return stable machine-readable errors; partner events are signed, replay-safe and deduplicated; APIs are versioned with compatibility windows. Partner-side user deprovisioning has a contractual maximum latency per tier, while sponsor-side revocation of all sessions is independent of the partner. Rate limits protect sensitive business flows.
current_practice: Not established. Unbound is requirements-only with no production system, customers or operating evidence (unbound@9b38de47).
intended_practice: API rules per UNB-API-002..006, entitlements per UNB-XIN-SAS-001, deprovisioning per TVR-WID-006 and WG-2, versioning per WG-8.
provable: Nothing operational. Only requirement text exists in unbound@9b38de47 (requirements/baseline/baseline.jsonl); no implementation, test execution or operating evidence.
customer_statement: Planned, not available today: partner APIs would be request-only, entitlement-checked, idempotent and signed, with bounded deprovisioning latency. Unbound has no production deployment; this describes intended design only.

title: Partner certification, suspension and exit
status_rationale: Specified only in Unbound requirements (UNB-TEN-011, UNB-GAP-025, TVR-WID-003, WG-6); no implementation, test or operating evidence exists.
target_answer: Partners are onboarded through a governed plan with certification of their integration, including copy review and a combined host-plus-widget accessibility test. Partner suspension stops new launches and new commands while accepted commands proceed under sponsor review and donors are informed through a sponsor channel. Partner exit runs as a PartnerExit case (notification, donor outreach, elections, proposed transfers, sponsor decisions, execution, reconciliation) in which funds move only as individual sponsor-authorized outbound grants with eligibility, sanctions and hold checks, and each partner has an exportable, evidence-complete dataset.
